title: Lift an infusion pump that has slid down its IV pole back to the tape mark and turn its pole clamp tight
justification: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131, about 1.35M, whose tasks include 'set up equipment') and registered nurses (29-1141, about 3.3M) mount infusion pumps on poles and move them between poles at every transfer. A pole clamp that is not turned tight lets the 1.4 kg pump slide down and swing round, dragging its line and leaving the pole top-heavy at the wrong height. Fixing it takes two hands: one holds the pump at height and square, while the other turns the clamp knob, whose torque also tries to twist the pump.
fault: The pump has slid down to the pole's lower collar, 8 cm above the bench, and turned 35 degrees about the pole. Its clamp knob is two turns loose.
instruction: This pump has slipped down its pole. Fix it back at the tape mark with its screen facing you.
objects: IV pole stub, fixed (like the accepted Alaris task's stub): chromed steel tube 25 mm across, from the bench to 60 cm, at x 33, y 0, with blue tape from 24 to 26 cm and a steel collar at 8 cm. Infusion pump: SimReady pump_infusion_a01 at real size (about 20 x 13 x 22 cm, grey ABS, carry handle on top), mass set to 1.4 kg; replace it with a custom mesh if the asset's shape is unsuitable. Pole clamp, custom mechkit, on the pump's back. The pump rides the pole on a prismatic joint (vertical) and a revolute joint (about the pole). Their friction drives scale with clamp tightness: free below half a turn past contact, locked from 1.5 turns. The knob has four lobes, is 6 cm across, sits on the pump's left side with its axis along the clamp screw (horizontal), and turns on a damped revolute. Distractors (SimReady): syringe_a02 at x 16, y -22; device_blood_pressure_monitor_a01 at x 18, y 24; disinfectant_b01 at x 40, y -24.
skill: One arm holds a 1.4 kg device by its carry handle (top-down) at a set height and square, against gravity and against the knob's twisting torque. The other turns the knob three turns by pressing its lobes down one after another and regrasping, like turning a wheel by its spokes.
scoring: From poses and the knob's joint (real trial: a ruler to the tape, a protractor on the pump face, and a hand check that it does not slide). Locked: knob 1.5 turns or more past contact. On mark: clamp centre within 1.5 cm of the tape centre. Facing: screen within 10 deg of facing the arms. End: grippers 3 cm or more from pump and pole, and the pump moving under 2 mm and 1 deg over 3 s. Whole-run latch F: the pump fell (downward faster than 0.6 m/s) or left the pole. Score 0 if F is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 locked, on mark and facing; 0.5 locked within 6 cm and 30 deg; 0.2 locked anywhere else; 0 not locked.
nearest: 'Load an IV set into an Alaris pump module' (accepted) works on a pump that is already clamped to a pole stub. 'Add clamp-a-flask-on-a-lab-stand task' (pending) tightens a clamp on a vertical rod. 'Fix a copper tube in two self-closing pipe clamps' (rejected). This task re-clamps the device's own clamp while holding its weight.
risks: This is the weakest of the eight. Its skill is close to the pending lab-stand clamp, and reviewers may call mounting a pump a supporting activity. Turning a horizontal-axis knob by pressing its lobes top-down is plausible, but it is not how a nurse turns one. 1.4 kg is near the arm's payload with the arm reaching upward. The SimReady pump's geometry is unknown until it is checked with simready_info.py.
